:::{#exm-self-outer-product-psd}
#### A quadratic form in a self outer product

For $\vx = (1, 2)$,
[the example of a self outer product](linear-algebra.qmd#exm-self-outer-product)
found $\soprod{\vx} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$,
which is [symmetric](#def-symmetric-matrix).
Take $\vecf{w} = (2, -1)$.
The [quadratic form](#def-quadratic-form) in $\soprod{\vx}$ at $\vecf{w}$ is

$$
\ba
\qform{\soprod{\vx}}{\vecf{w}}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(definition of the quadratic form)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(} 1 \cd 2 + 2 \cd (-1) = 0 \text{ and } 2 \cd 2 + 4 \cd (-1) = 0 \text{)}
\\
&= 0
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

The quadratic form is $0$ here, which is not negative,
as @cor-self-outer-product-psd says.
It is not positive either,
because $\vecf{w}$ is orthogonal to $\vx$.
